data.title: FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem (FFR) Announces parent company Faraday Future (FFAI) Ownership of Approximately $41 Million in FFR Equity
data.description:
Reinforcing Long-Term Commitment to the Growth of FFR and filed a Schedule 14C with the Securities and Exchange Commission

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. () ("FFR" or the "Company"), a U.S.-based Embodied AI ("EAI") robotics company, today announced it had filed a preliminary Schedule 14C with the Securities and Exchange Commission, which includes pro forma financial information for the acquired robotics business, as well as additional disclosures related to FFR's acquisition of the robotics business of Faraday Future (), including transaction details, ownership structure, and other relevant information for stockholders and investors, marking the completion of all material matters required of both parties post deal closing.

As of November 25, 2026, FFAI beneficially owned approximately 14.7 million shares of FFR common stock, representing approximately 53% of FFR's 27.7 million shares currently outstanding. Following the issuance of shares contemplated by FFR's acquisition of the robotics business, FFAI is expected to own approximately 80.1 million shares, or approximately 75% of FFR's anticipated 106.2 million outstanding shares. All newly issued FFR shares received by FFAI in the transaction are subject to an 18‑month lock-up period. Based on FFR's closing market price on November 25, 2026, the implied value of FFAI's expected ownership position would be approximately $41 million.

The holding reflects Faraday Future's continued commitment to supporting the development of the FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem and aligns FFAI's interests with those of FFR stockholders as the company advances the commercialization of its robotics, AI, and intelligent automation solutions.

"FFAI's substantial ownership position reflects its continuing strategic alignment with FFR," said YT Jia, Global CEO of FFAI and FFR. "We believe FFR is uniquely positioned at the intersection of artificial intelligence and robotics, with a growing portfolio of technologies, products, strategic partnerships, and commercialization initiatives designed to create long-term shareholder value."

FFR has continued to expand its robotics ecosystem through advancements across its key business pillars, including Physical AI Devices, the Physical AI Brain and Developer Platform, Industry Productivity Solutions, and the Physical AI Data Factory. The company has also been pursuing commercialization opportunities across enterprise, education, service, and industrial applications.

FFR's strategy is supported by several key factors:

  • Expanding market demand for intelligent robotics and AI-enabled automation solutions;
  • Continued development of FFR's integrated robotics ecosystem;
  • Growth in strategic partnerships and commercial deployments;
  • Increasing opportunities to monetize robotics solutions in K-12 education sector, security and surveillance among others; and
  • The potential for long-term value creation as the robotics industry continues to mature globally.

FFAI will continue to evaluate opportunities to further support FFR's strategic initiatives, subject to market conditions, corporate requirements, and applicable regulations.

About FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc.

FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. () is a U.S.-based Embodied AI robotics company focused on the research and development, manufacturing, commercialization and deployment of intelligent robotic technologies, products and industry solutions. FFR is building a "Four-Core Full-Stack" AI ecosystem covering the full lifecycle of robotics, consisting of Physical AI Brain & Developer Platform, Physical AI Devices, Physical AI Industry Productivity Solutions, and Physical AI Data Factory. Guided by the technology and product philosophy of "One Brain, Multi-forms, Multi-capabilities," FFR aims to empower humanoid, biomimetic, and other robotic form factors through a unified Physical AI Brain, while continuously expanding their multi-task and multi-scenario capabilities. The ecosystem is designed to support the full robotics lifecycle, including R&D, deployment, data collection and training, operations, and commercial applications. FFR also operates RoboShare, a robot-sharing and services platform. To learn more, visit www.ff.com.

data.title: Dogness Showcases New AI-Powered Pet Products at CIPS 2026, Highlighting Global Market Expansion
data.description:
DONGGUAN, China, Nov. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Dogness (International) Corporation ("Dogness" or the "Company") (), a developer and manufacturer of a comprehensive line of Dogness-branded, OEM and private-label pet products, announced that it showcased its new AI-powered smart pet feeders, alongside its established pet product portfolio, at the 30th China International Pet Show (CIPS 2026), held from November 12 to 15 in Guangzhou, China. The exhibition underscores the Company's continued advancement of its AI-driven smart pet care strategy and its global distribution. Through its distribution network across 35 countries and regions, Dogness aims to commercialize its AI-powered pet products and capture new growth opportunities in the smart pet care industry.

Extensive Global Distribution Network Supports AI Product Commercialization

Dogness's channel network now covers 35 countries and regions worldwide. It sells through global retailers and specialized pet channels including Walmart, Costco, Petco and Pet Valu, online platforms such as Amazon and Chewy, as well as brand and industry partners like Velcro. This broad network and the Company's long-standing relationships provide a foundation for presenting products, gathering market feedback and exploring new collaborations. They also support Dogness's efforts to introduce its new AI products to different markets and adapt its product portfolio to local needs, strengthening its relationships with major international retailers.

Driving AI Innovation in Smart Pet Care Through a Structured Matrix of AI Products

While strengthening its established pet supplies business, Dogness continues to expand the development and production of AI-enabled pet products. The Company continues to invest in R&D for intelligent functions and products designed for specific pet care needs, pursuing a two-track approach that combines an established product foundation with continued AI innovation.

  • New AI Products: Advancing the AI Strategy through Smart Feeding

At CIPS 2026, Dogness showcased the F01B and F10B AI feeders, allowing attendees to explore smart feeding and scenario-based interaction features through hands-on demonstrations. The 3.6-liter F10B, built with Google Gemini, features a high-definition night-vision camera and AI-powered behavior recognition that alerts owners to unusual activity through the Dogness mobile app. The F01B offers a larger 8-liter capacity in a distinct design. AI feeders are an important entry point within the Company's expanding portfolio of AI pet products. Dogness continues to invest in R&D and refine products around real-world pet care needs, advancing the application of AI capabilities in everyday feeding scenarios.

More importantly, Dogness's AI strategy is not a collection of standalone devices but a scenario-driven product matrix. Its technical strengths are reflected in three areas: first, scenario-based interaction capabilities developed around high-frequency pet care scenarios including feeding, interaction and location tracking; second, integrated hardware-software-scenario design that enables AI features to deliver a seamless user experience throughout real-world usage journeys; and third, sustained R&D and iteration capabilities, underpinned by the Company's continued investment in intelligent function development and scenario-based product pipeline reserves. AI feeders serve as the primary entry point, as the product matrix extends into location-tracking use cases, with AI-enabled water fountains in the pipeline to form a multi-scenario AI product matrix covering feeding, hydration and location tracking.

  • Established Product Portfolio as a Robust Foundation for AI-Driven Growth

At CIPS 2026, Dogness also presented quick-release pet leashes, the slow-recovery R06 retractable leash, paw cleaner cups, training mats and reflective collars, covering everyday walking, cleaning, training and visibility needs.

The established portfolio delivers four key pillars supporting Dogness's AI product development: an established customer base and repeat-purchase relationships that create a natural on-ramp for AI products; brand recognition that lowers market education costs for new AI offerings; an integrated, in-house supply chain covering design and R&D, material sourcing, manufacturing and quality control, which supports production of AI products with consistent quality and effective cost control; and existing sales channels, including distributor networks, retail outlets and e-commerce operations, to support the distribution and promotion of AI products.

Furthermore, Dogness's traditional and AI businesses unlock opportunities for cross-selling and mutual promotion. Channel credibility and user relationships built through its established product lineup help AI products gain market traction. In turn, AI products elevate the brand's technological positioning and customer value, reinforcing the established product portfolio. As such, Dogness has built a growth framework wherein its established product portfolio stabilizes the core business and its structured AI product matrix is intended to drive incremental growth.

Silong Chen, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Dogness, commented: "CIPS 2026 enables us to leverage our well-established worldwide sales network and customer base, supported by end-to-end R&D and manufacturing systems, to further advance our strategic transformation from a traditional global pet products manufacturer into a global AI-powered smart pet care technology company, and accelerate the global commercialization of AI-powered pet products."

About Dogness

Dogness (International) Corporation was founded in 2003 from the belief that dogs and cats are important, well-loved family members. Through its smart products, hygiene products, health and wellness products, and leash products, Dogness' technology simplifies pet lifestyles and enhances the relationship between pets and pet caregivers. The Company ensures industry-leading quality through its fully integrated vertical supply chain and world-class research and development capabilities, which have resulted in over 200 patents and patents pending. Dogness products reach families worldwide through global chain stores and distributors. For more information, please visit: ir.dogness.com.

data.title: Tobacco Firm Altria Explores $30 Billion Acquisition Of Imperial Brands
data.description:
Tobacco giant Altria Group (MO) is reportedly exploring a $30 billion U.S. acquisition of rival Imperial Brands (IMB).

American Altria, which makes Marlboro cigarettes, is considering an all-cash offer for British rival Imperial Brands but is also in discussions with a third party about breaking up Imperial to mitigate antitrust concerns around a potential deal.

Media reports say that Japan Tobacco (JAPAY) could be a potential partner of Altria on the purchase of Imperial Brands.

Imperial Brands is currently valued at 22.6 billion British pounds ($30 billion U.S.) based on its market capitalization.

Altria has not publicly announced any acquisition. According to media reports, the tobacco company’s board of directors is exploring its options.

Shares of Imperial, which makes Winston cigarettes, rose 15% on Nov. 26 after media reports surfaced concerning a potential acquisition.

Altria’s stock has risen 30% in the past 12 months to trade at $76.28 U.S. per share.

data.title: Czech lower house approves windfall tax on refineries, will hit Orlen
data.description:
The lower house of the Czech parliament approved on Friday imposing a windfall tax on refineries for 2026 and 2027, which will affect the Czech operations of Poland's energy group Orlen , the owner of the Czech Republic's two oil refineries.

  • The tax will be applied in 2026 and 2027, and the Finance Ministry expects it to raise at least 5.5 billion crowns ($247 million) for 2026, Finance Minister Alena Schillerova said

  • The government argues that refineries are making windfall profit from a jump in the spread between crude oil prices and oil products this year amid the US-Israeli war with Iran

  • The tax is to be set at 50% of the increase in gross refining margins versus 2025

  • Orlen Unipetrol has strongly opposed the tax, saying it will undermine its ability to invest in the modernisation of Czech operations

  • Orlen Unipetrol argues it posted losses in the past two years and has not paid dividends since Orlen's takeover in 2018

  • The government aims to find revenue to compensate for cuts in excise tax on automobile fuels it adopted earlier this year amid soaring prices

  • Poland, home of the parent Orlen group, has introduced a windfall tax on fuel sold by refineries, estimated to yield some 4 billion zloty ($982 million) of revenue this year

  • The Czech bill will now go to the upper house, where the opposition holds a majority and may vote to return the bill to the lower house. The government has enough votes in the lower house to overturn a veto by the upper house, although it may have to rush to complete the process before the end of the year

($1 = 22.2550 Czech crowns)

data.title: Stock Futures Jump as AI Trade Set for Rebound — Update
data.description:
By Joe Stonor

U.S. stock indexes are poised to open in the green for a shortened trading session Friday, as the artificial-intelligence trade rebounds at the end of a volatile week.

Nasdaq futures traded 2% higher, while contracts tied to the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.4% and 1.2%, respectively. If the gains hold to market close, the indexes will close a choppy week with gains of more than 4% each. Still, they remain well below their recent highs: The S&P 500 and Dow are each over 6% below their early October peaks, while the Nasdaq, down more than 14% over the same period, is still in a correction.

Signs of a rebound follow choppy trade earlier in the week. Stocks across the AI ecosystem rallied premarket, with Nvidia gaining over 3%, while chip makers and data-center providers looked set for strong opens. However, the AI trade isn't out of the woods yet, Amati Global Investors fund manager Mikhail Zverev said.

"We still haven't got answers to the biggest questions we are asking," the fund manager said. Concerns include "higher interest rates and the expanding cost of funding for the AI buildout," Zverev added.

Gains in the U.S. premarket followed a bullish session in Asia. South Korea's memory-chip-dominated Kospi jumped 4.3%, while stock indexes in Shanghai and Hong Kong rose after Chinese authorities reiterated their support for capital markets. European equity indexes rallied at the open, with AI-related stocks leading the charge. The continent's Stoxx 600 index rose 0.9% in afternoon trade.

Improved sentiment in equity markets bled into metals, too. Silver contracts jumped more than 9% to $43.68 a troy ounce, while gold futures added 3.6% to trade around $3,660 an ounce.

Oil prices continued to rise, with most-traded Brent crude contracts for February delivery nudging up 0.3% to trade close to $92 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate contract added 1.7% to trade around $85.10 a barrel.

Treasurys weakened amid investors' shift back to risk and hardened expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike next month. Ten-year yields rose more than 5.5 basis points to trade above 4.900%, while two-year yields rose toward 4.700%. The Fed enters a blackout period on Saturday ahead of its December meeting, with expectations for a quarter-point rise priced in at 99%, according to LSEG.

The dollar edged higher against a basket of global currencies but remained below highs hit earlier this week. Bitcoin was helped by broader ebullient market sentiment, rising 1.5% to trade around $61,670.

Spanish voters head to the polls on Sunday as Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez looks to stay in power. Next week, Nvidia's reinstated Chief Executive Jensen Huang will appear in front of Congress on Tuesday and Wednesday.

data.title: Carlsberg plans an IPO for its India unit
data.description:
Carlsberg India, the country's second-largest brewer, plans to sell up to 86.4M shares, or about 15% of the company, through an entirely secondary offering. That will mean an infusion of cash for Danish parent Carlsberg . The latest reports say the IPO could raise as much as $600M at a $4B valuation. The IPO could launch as early as December.

The Securities and Exchange Board of India approved the IPO, which had been filed under its confidential pre-filing route. Carlsberg India reported revenue of 87.09B rupees for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026. The company runs seven breweries and holds a 21.9% market share across 16 key states and union territories in India.

data.title: Cautious consumers gear up for Black Friday as inflation woes bite
data.description:
Key points:
  • Consumers seen spending despite cost-of-living gloom
  • Target, Kohl's, rivals point to belt-tightening
  • Toy prices surge on supply chain woes, including plastics
  • AI looms as wild card

By Nicholas P. Brown, Juveria Tabassum and Danielle Kaye

Neither high fuel prices nor stubborn inflation are expected to stop US shoppers from spending robustly as their turkey hangovers wear off on Black Friday. But below healthy top-line forecasts lie signs of stress.

Holiday spending — which unofficially begins on Black Friday — is seen topping last year's strong figures by 4%-6%, several economic forecasts show. But most of the gains will be attributable to inflation which, at 3.8%, is about a percentage point higher than in each of the last two years.

Consumers spent about $7.1 billion online on Thursday - the US Thanksgiving holiday - a 10.4% jump over last year, according to a report from Adobe. Fueled by big discounts on electronics, toys and apparel, spending edged past Adobe's initial expectations of $6.9 billion.

The National Retail Federation sees November-December holiday retail sales rising 4.2% year-over-year, to just above $1 trillion. The Mastercard Economics Institute and EY Parthenon each forecast sales to rise more than 5%.

Eventual final results often beat pre-holiday estimates. Still, consumer sentiment remains shaky. This month, voters punished US President Donald Trump for an Iran War that's pushed the cost of living higher, handing Democrats sweeping electoral victories.

A November survey by the National Retail Federation found that 82% of consumers are taking steps to manage holiday costs, like buying less expensive gifts.

Los Angeles resident Felicia Cox, 50, said that while her holiday spending will be roughly stable, inflation is impacting how she thinks. "I want to get more gifts that people will actually use or need," said Cox, a sales representative, while browsing in an L.A. Marshalls last week. "I feel like people aren't able to afford as much stuff."

Worries aside, some 87% of 1,200 consumers surveyed by Deloitte in October planned to participate in the five-day shopping period from Thanksgiving through "Cyber Monday," November 30 — the highest in a decade, according to Deloitte.

"People like to spend during the holidays," even when there's a "persisting undercurrent of stress,” said Katie Thomas, who leads the Kearney Consumer Institute, part of global consulting firm Kearney.

Online spending on Black Friday is expected to jump 9.2% from a year ago to $12.9 billion, driven by increased usage of Buy Now Pay Later options, and by steep discounts on televisions, toys and furniture, according to Adobe's initial Black Friday forecast.

However, spending is not uniform, and middle- and lower-income shoppers — who have been trading down for months — were more likely than wealthy ones to spend less, according to the Kearney survey.

Target , Dollar Tree and Kohl's have all pointed to belt-tightening during recent earnings calls. Kohl's CEO Michael Bender on Tuesday cited an "increasingly choiceful" consumer that is "looking to stretch every dollar."

Holiday spending forecasts mostly predated the recent stock market correction that followed the midterms, turmoil at chipmaker Nvidia , and mounting concerns around an AI bubble. The decline could dampen the wealth effect that has seen affluent shoppers splurge on gadgets and accessories, UBS analysts said in a note on Tuesday.

TOYS TAKE A HIT

Higher input costs, particularly from petrol derivatives like plastic, are hitting some products more than others.

Prices of toys — generally high in plastic — have risen 13.2% since the start of the year, pushing Barbie maker Mattel this month to cut its annual forecast as consumers balked at higher costs.

Some unlikely products are buoying the toy category. Best Buy and Target have both flagged trading cards — including Pokemon and Magic: The Gathering products — as a key growth driver. Squishy NeeDoh toys were selling for $24.99 on Amazon in October, nearly triple the price a year earlier on hot demand, according to e-commerce marketing platform Omnisend.

Gaming was a hot category amid the much-awaited launch of Rockstar Games' "Grand Theft Auto VI" video game last week, the Adobe report said.

Toy maker Learning Resources Inc — a plaintiff in lawsuits that overturned Trump's tariffs — is seeing demand roughly flat, said CEO Rick Woldenberg, though he added it's hard to predict demand before Black Friday.

"People can't shop until they have their turkey," Woldenberg said.

AI could also scramble the year's shopping dynamics. As shoppers use AI to find bargains or even complete purchases — and retailers become increasingly adept at altering price quickly through AI — the deepest discounts could come closer to Christmas, as consumers and retailers both wait out the market, said Ryan Orabone, a consultant at Spaulding Ridge.

"My advice to shoppers is to be patient," he said. "Don't jump on the first deal you see."

data.title: Global fashion brands shift orders from Bangladesh to India amid unrest
data.description:
Key points:
  • Zara, H&M, M&S, Celio shift Bangladesh orders, mostly to India
  • Brands divert $254 million in orders as factories shut
  • Bangladesh unrest causes over $400 million in production losses
  • Rising wages, energy shortages erode Bangladesh's cost edge
  • Temporary order shifts risk becoming long-term sourcing moves

By Ruma Paul

Global fashion retailers including Zara and H&M shifted nearly a tenth of their monthly orders from Bangladesh to other Asian manufacturing hubs in the first half of November, as labour unrest disrupted production and rising costs eroded the country's competitive edge, three factory owners said.

Between November 1 and 18, brands diverted about $254 million worth of orders from Bangladesh, with most moving to neighbouring India, the owners said, a shift that represents a major blow to a key pillar of Bangladesh's economy and could extend beyond the current unrest.

Industry leaders have said rising wages, energy shortages and political uncertainty have weakened the low-cost advantage that helped make Bangladesh the world's second apparel exporter after China, prompting global brands to diversify sourcing.

The protests have caused more than $400 million in production losses, according to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), in an industry that accounts for more than 80% of Bangladesh's export earnings and nearly 40% of its manufacturing jobs.

VIETNAM, CAMBODIA AND INDONESIA ALSO BENEFIT

India has emerged as the biggest beneficiary, while buyers are also looking to Vietnam, Cambodia and Indonesia to reduce supply-chain risks and improve delivery reliability, industry leaders said.

Those pressures intensified on Wednesday when Bangladesh approved a 36% increase in the minimum wage for garment workers, the smallest rise in four decades.

The increase fell well short of workers' demands to more than double wages, triggering fresh clashes with police even as Abdur Rahman Tarafder, secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Employment, said the wage increase was "satisfactory" and that he hoped all workers would resume work from Saturday.

Industry leaders said the increase would nevertheless narrow Bangladesh's labour-cost advantage over India, although union groups argue the wages remain low by global industry standards.

Babul Akhter, a union leader and workers' representative on the government-appointed wage board, said brands should not use the unrest to justify shifting orders out of Bangladesh.

He said retailers already factor political instability and labour unrest into sourcing decisions, making such moves "hard to justify" and raising "serious doubts" whether the unrest was more than an excuse.

Factory owners, speaking on condition of anonymity because of concerns about their relationships with international buyers, said the unrest had prompted Zara, H&M, Marks & Spencer, Celio and other global brands to divert orders, with India receiving the bulk of the business.

Zara owner Inditex declined to comment on Reuters’ questions, while M&S , H&M and Celio did not respond to requests for comment.

Indian textile shares rallied after the Reuters report, with Gokaldas Exports jumping as much as 11% and Trident gaining about 5%. Other potential beneficiaries, including Welspun Living , KPR Mill and Vardhman Textiles rose around 2% each.

M. Mohiuddin Chowdhury, a director of the BGMEA, said higher wages, utility and raw-material costs were adding to pressure on manufacturers "at a time when buyers are demanding lower prices and competition from rival sourcing countries is intensifying".

MORE BUSINESS AT RISK

Factory owners said the bigger concern was that diversions of business could become permanent.

Persistent energy shortages, exacerbated by the Middle East crisis, have added to production disruptions and forced some factories to rely on more expensive alternative power sources.

But Chowdhury said that price became secondary when brands were under pressure to meet strict delivery deadlines.

India can offer buyers a delivery advantage of about a week, while Vietnam and Cambodia can cut lead times by as much as 15 days, Chowdhury said.

Rival sourcing hubs can typically complete production and delivery within 60 to 90 days, compared with about 120 days in Bangladesh, he added.

The disruptions have also created production backlogs, with manufacturers around Dhaka losing an estimated 20 to 25 production days. Some are considering overtime and costly air freight to meet delivery commitments.

Khan Monirul Alam, managing director of Alps Apparels Group, which mainly supplies European brands, said the unrest was already hitting new business.

"Since November 1, most of my buyers have stopped placing orders because of the unrest," Alam said. "They are telling us our orders have been shifted, postponed or cancelled and that they have already found alternative solutions."

Political tensions surrounding former prime minister Sheikh Hasina's possible return to Dhaka from India have added to concerns about further disruption.

Industry leaders said restoring stability and uninterrupted production would be critical to retaining international buyers. Chowdhury warned that orders shifted elsewhere during periods of instability might not return even after conditions improved.

"The challenge is restoring buyers' confidence before temporary shifts become long-term sourcing decisions," he said. "Brands have options. They will not wait for us if instability persists."

data.title: The Week in Oil: Crude on Track for Weekly Gains As Middle East Attacks Worry Market
data.description:
By Giulia Petroni

Here is a look at what happened in oil markets during the week of Nov. 23-27 and what traders will be watching in the days ahead.

OVERVIEW: Oil prices are on track for weekly gains on Friday after three consecutive weekly losses as continuing attacks on Middle Eastern shipping and Saudi infrastructure raised regional supply concerns. Front-month Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, is down 0.3% to $96.35 a barrel, while WTI futures rise 1.5% to $84.95 a barrel.

MACRO: Major U.S. indexes are poised to finish higher after a volatile week marked by AI jitters. "Stock markets around the world are hoping to put the recent turmoil behind them, staging a decent rebound as the week and month draw to a close," said XM analyst Raffi Boyadjian. "The shortened trading week in the United States due to the Thanksgiving holiday has likely helped in restoring some calm to equity markets."

This week's economic data indicated persistent inflation, resilient growth, and a solid labor market. Focus now shifts to the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decision next month, with traders already pricing in a 25-basis-point hike.

GEOPOLITICAL RISKS: With no meaningful progress in U.S.-Iran negotiations, regional tensions remain high. Continued attacks on vessels in the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman have kept maritime security and potential supply disruptions in focus.

Oil supplies have remained largely unaffected, according to Commerzbank analysts. However, that could change if Saudi Arabia is forced to reduce oil exports through Ras Tanura, especially as Houthi militants also threaten export terminals on the Red Sea.

Earlier this week, the Houthis claimed an attack on Ras Tanura, which is Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery. Meanwhile, a separate strike on the country's Jazan refinery sparked a fire and temporarily halted some operations, while a drone attack in Kuwait killed two Italian technicians.

SUPPLY AND DEMAND: Middle Eastern oil flows remain significantly below prewar levels, with Strait of Hormuz transits at just 31% of the preconflict baseline, according to preliminary data from Kpler.

Iraqi crude exports remain relatively strong despite delays to some November and December shipments, which Kpler attributed to oversold cargoes rather than falling production. Still, the delays have raised concerns over the reliability of prompt Middle Eastern supply, highlighting the market's sensitivity to short-term disruptions even in an otherwise well-supplied regional market, said Alex Booth, head of research at the data provider.

In the U.S., crude oil inventories rose for a third consecutive week as refineries increased capacity utilization, according to the latest Energy Information Administration data. Gasoline and distillate fuel stocks also climbed.

WHAT'S AHEAD: Attention now turns to Sunday's OPEC+ meeting, with some analysts expecting the group to hold current production quotas steady through January. With existing production agreements approaching their year-end deadline, key members of the group must decide how much oil each country can sustainably produce, and how much the cartel should collectively pump next year.

"It is quite possible that Sunday's OPEC+ meeting will end without a final decision and that current production quotas will initially remain in place, as OPEC delegates have indicated," said Commerzbank analyst Barbara Lambrecht. "With the exception of Iraq, production in most OPEC+ countries remains well below existing quotas, while some countries, including Russia, are unable to raise output any further."

Investors will also be watching for Saudi Arabia's official selling prices, which are set to be disclosed next week.

On the U.S. economic calendar, the ISM manufacturing and services PMI readings will provide further insight into the strength of the economy, while Jolts, ADP employment and weekly jobless claims will offer clues on labor market conditions ahead of Friday's November nonfarm payrolls report.

Write to Giulia Petroni at giulia.petroni@wsj.com

data.title: Bitcoin, Ether Rebound as Markets Stabilize — Update
data.description:
By Joseph Wilkins

Bitcoin rebounded above $61,000 on Friday as Asian markets stabilized and risk appetite returned to cryptocurrencies.

Bitcoin was 1.1% higher at $61,465, while ether gained 1% to $1,720. U.S. stock futures rose Friday following a break for Thanksgiving, with Asian markets taking cues. South Korea's Kospi rose more than 4%, with chip heavyweights SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics jumping 6.4% and 4.5%, respectively.

Bitcoin's 90-day correlation to the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq-100 has rebuilt since reaching a year-to-date low in September, Block Scholes analyst Thahbib Rahman wrote in a note. Bitcoin's current correlation is 53% to the S&P 500 and 54% to the Nasdaq-100, up from 37% and 36% at the end of October.

Rahman said the flagship cryptocurrency could remain stuck as long as fears around the durability of the AI trade persist and drag down U.S. stocks.

Write to Joseph Wilkins at joseph.wilkins@wsj.com

data.title: India's Adani Group targets capex of nearly $24 billion in FY27, CFO Singh says
data.description:
By Dharamraj Dhutia

India's Adani Group is looking at around 2.2 trillion rupees ($23.72 billion) in capital expenditure in fiscal 2027, its chief finance officer Jugeshinder Singh said on Friday, as the ports-to-power conglomerate expands operations across sectors.

  • Speaking at Trust Group's debt capital market summit in Mumbai, Singh said the group will invest $10 billion in data centres over the next four years

  • Earlier this month, executives of the conglomerate, one of India's largest, said the group was planning to invest more than $120 billion in capital expenditure over the next five years across its core infrastructure businesses and emerging growth platforms

  • Singh also said that Adani Ports would tap the dollar debt market through a public issuance in the next financial year, starting April, and is considering issuing 20-year papers

  • The group set its borrowing target in the range of 1.3 trillion rupees to 1.4 trillion rupees each across this financial year and the next

  • Singh added that the group plans to source 75% to 80% of its borrowings from local markets, while raising the remaining share from global markets in the coming years

  • The CFO confirmed that the group's flagship firm Adani Enterprises would go ahead with its fourth public issue in December, while Adani Power is expected to become a larger borrower in the rupee bond market in the future
